transcript:
Header: Q3->Q4 Roadmap Launch Readiness / Handoff
Date: 2026-08-20 10:00 PDT
Duration: ~78 minutes
Attendees: Ava, Marco, Priya, Elena, Carlos, Samir

Summary: quick recap of Q3 shipped items, gaps to close for Q4 dedicated launch, review of July 31 KV-cache incident and mitigations, assign owners for rollout and docs.

00:00:00 - Ava: ok team, thanks for joining, I'll kick off with a 5 minute recap of what shipped in Q3 and then we do the incident review and handoff.
00:00:15 - Marco: yep, sounds good. I think we should start with the dedicated autoscaler notes, there were a couple follow ups from infra.
00:00:30 - Ava: right, autoscaler 2.1 shipped last week, but we still have the burst policy flag to finish. Carlos is on that.
00:00:45 - Carlos: yep, the burst flag PR is in review, I expect it merged later today, it's mostly docs and a config override for reserved pools.
00:01:12 - Samir: just flagging one caveat - the PR changes the allocation heuristics and we've seen a small jitter in tail latency in staging, nothing huge but needs watching.
00:01:30 - Priya: that's what triggered the staging failover runs, I can rerun them with the latest kernel and capture p95/p99.
00:01:45 - Ava: perfect, add that to action items.

00:05:20 - Ava: moving to the KV-cache incident on July 31 - quick postmortem, we had an eviction storm when a large customer ran heavy long-context workloads; cache churn plus a hot shard caused OOMs on two nodes, autoscaler didn't react quickly enough and that pushed some requests to fallback model variants.
00:05:45 - Marco: yeah to add detail, the eviction policy was LRU but at high churn the metadata lock became contended; we saw stall on the cache maintenance thread.
00:06:05 - Samir: transcripts from the incident show some retries piling up, and the fallback route increased latency by ~400ms on average for those requests.
00:06:25 - Priya: the mitigation we applied was increasing the cache slab and enabling async eviction; that reduced the contention but it's not a permanent fix.
00:06:40 - Ava: so long term we want a two-pronged approach: kernel-level lock removal (Samir), and a graceful degrade path in the router to avoid avalanching. Carlos/Marco can you scope the rollout?
00:06:58 - Carlos: I'll put together a runbook; immediate short term is to increase slab sizes in prod and add circuit-breaker thresholds in the router. Long term is a refactor to move maintenance off the hot path.

00:12:10 - Elena: for launch comms we need to be explicit about what customers will see if we hit cache pressure - do we mention fallbacks in the SLA doc?
00:12:28 - Ava: yes include it as an example and the mitigation steps; PMM should draft the wording so it doesn't sound like a reliability promise.
00:12:40 - Elena: got it, I'll draft language and link to the postmortem.

00:15:05 - Marco: quick note on benchmarking - Samir, we need numbers for the quantized profiles across p4d and a100, and the sequence length distributions. Sales wants to see cost per 1k tokens at 2k vs 8k vs 16k.
00:15:28 - Samir: on it, I'll run the matrix next week; do we have a canonical prompt set?
00:15:35 - Ava: use the q3-q4 benchmark sheet in Drive, link in chat: https://drive.redwood/roadmap/q3-q4-benchmarks (note: link may be internal). Include top customer prompt families.
00:15:50 - Samir: perfect, I'll upload results to that sheet.

00:20:00 - Priya: on the security front, KMS rotation for dedicated customers requires SOC2 sign-off and one appendix for the SSO flow, security has a checklist. We need to ensure the HSM integration path is validated for the Private customers.
00:20:20 - Carlos: PCI-like customers asked about in transit vs at rest; we already have envelope encryption but SAs requested an audit of KMS access patterns.
00:20:35 - Priya: I'll coordinate with Security to produce the access audit and the design doc by next week.

00:23:50 - Ava: can we talk about rollout strategy - canary percentages, metrics to watch, and automatic rollback triggers. I proposed an initial canary at 5% traffic for 48 hours with p95 latency and error-rate thresholds.
00:24:10 - Marco: 5% is fine, but for kernel changes we should do progressive canary: 1% for 12h, 5% for 48h, then 20% for a day before full. Also add a blue-green possibility if things go sideways.
00:24:35 - Carlos: I'll add those steps to the runbook and include the rollback playbook. We should also capture feature flags to disable slab increases dynamically.
00:24:50 - Samir: we need telemetry hooks - KV eviction rates, maintenance thread latency, and per-node memory headroom. Those should be part of the canary dashboard.

00:30:05 - Elena: marketing needs an ETA for the launch window so we can schedule webinars; what's the realistic earliest?
00:30:20 - Ava: if we close the remaining security and benchmark work by end of August, we can target a soft launch early October. Rough timeline: September for canaries and internal beta, first week of October external launch.
00:30:45 - Elena: ok we'll plan comms around that and prepare support playbooks.

00:33:10 - Samir: there's also a dependency with the quantization toolchain update - new kernels shipped in runtime v3.4 require small model conversion changes. If conversion scripts break, that could delay rollout.
00:33:28 - Marco: we need a smoke test that validates converted model correctness (sampling tests) before canary. Samir can own that.
00:33:40 - Samir: yep, adding smoke tests to the benchmark job.

00:38:00 - Priya: incident response follow up - we should update on-call runbooks and include the KV-cache drill as a tabletop exercise next rotation.
00:38:15 - Carlos: agreed, I'll schedule the tabletop and invite SRE and runtime engineers.

00:42:05 - Ava: open issues / blockers: 1) Security sign-off on KMS up to SOC2 appendix; 2) Autoscaler tail-latency jitter research; 3) Quantized benchmark matrix; 4) Docs + pricing SKU update. Who owns each?
00:42:22 - Priya: security sign-off I'll take and coordinate with Security (owner Priya).
00:42:30 - Marco: autoscaler jitter Marco and Samir will pair.
00:42:40 - Samir: yep pairing on profiling.
00:42:45 - Carlos: I'll take docs/pricing coordination but need input from Sales Ops and Finance.

00:45:00 - Elena: also flagging support readiness - playbooks for rollback, and customer comm templates if we need to inform affected customers.
00:45:12 - Ava: add that to Elena's list.

00:50:30 - Carlos: runbook outline: preflight checklist, canary windows, monitoring thresholds, rollback steps, communications matrix, postmortem templates. Will include exact metrics and dashboard links.
00:51:00 - Ava: include links to monitoring dashboards; example: https://observability.redwood/dashboards/kv-cache-canary (internal)

00:55:00 - Marco: technical deep dive note: kernel-level lock removal is medium risk but high reward; if we can switch to lock-free maintenance and batch eviction we can reduce jitter significantly. Samir, can you estimate effort?
00:55:20 - Samir: rough estimate 3-4 sprints of focused work, but we can do incremental changes: async eviction first (small PR), then lock-free refactor. We'll hazard the first change in Q4 core runtime sprint.
00:55:40 - Marco: adds complexity to testing - needs strong regression suite.

01:02:10 - Priya: staging failover test details: I'll run traffic shapes that mimic the top 5 customer patterns, validate p95/p99 and error budget impact; will record the run and upload artifacts.
01:02:30 - Samir: please include the histograms and the request traces so we can pinpoint hotspots.

01:06:15 - Ava: ok let's recap decisions and owners - runbook and rollback: Carlos; bench matrix: Samir; security KMS audit: Priya; comms and FAQs: Elena; RACI and exec note: Ava. We agreed on progressive canary and the target soft launch early October.
01:06:45 - Carlos: I'll circulate updated runbook and schedule the tabletop by Friday.
01:07:00 - Ava: perfect. Anything else?
01:07:12 - Marco: nope.
01:07:20 - Elena: all good from marketing.
01:07:30 - Priya: thanks everyone.
01:07:45 - Ava: thanks team, meeting adjourned.

References/Artifacts mentioned: Drive benchmark sheet (internal): https://drive.redwood/roadmap/q3-q4-benchmarks ; runbook template: https://docs.redwood/runbooks/rollout-template ; observability dashboard (internal): https://observability.redwood/dashboards/kv-cache-canary

Notes on transcript quality: automated transcription with some name mis-attributions and occasional missing punctuation; content reviewed by Ava for action items.
